title: Per-result freshness + confidence signals
description:
Attach `_freshness ∈ {fresh, edited_uncommitted, stale_index}` to every result entry by comparing per-file mtime to the last parse timestamp. Aggregate into a `_meta.freshness` summary on each response.

Confidence is opt-in per tool — only meaningful for ranked queries (`sutra_find`, `sutra_grep`). Compute from top-1/top-2 score gap and identity-match presence.

**Session coordination note:** this touches every tool's response builder. Should be done as a single focused session — other simple-additions tasks land afterward and inherit the new metadata automatically. Avoid running this in parallel with any other simple-additions task to prevent merge conflicts on response shapes.

See docs/feature-ideas.md → "Per-result freshness + confidence".

acceptance_criteria.text: All ranked tools include _freshness on each result entry
Response root includes _meta.freshness summary (counts of fresh/edited/stale)

decisions: Per-entry freshness uses disk mtime vs FileRow.last_parsed — lightweight, no content hashing
SearchTier enum (Exact=1.0, Fts=0.6) — confidence formula embedded in JSON response for self-documentation
Backward-compatible: original handle() signatures preserved, new handle_with_freshness() variants used by MCP layer

messages.author: agent
messages.text:
All 4 acceptance criteria implemented and tested:
1. Per-entry _freshness on map, find, grep, hotspots, file_health (fresh/edited/stale based on disk mtime vs last_parsed)
2. _meta.freshness summary with fresh/edited/stale counts at response root
3. _meta.confidence on find and grep (score + tier + formula)
4. Confidence formula documented in the JSON response itself

New files: src/freshness.rs (module with FileStatus, FreshnessCounts, SearchTier, confidence_json)
Modified: db.rs (additive: find_symbols_by_name_tiered), find.rs, grep.rs, map.rs, hotspots.rs, file_health.rs, mcp.rs
Tests: 6 unit tests in freshness module + 7 new contract tests in mcp_contract_test.rs — all 160 tests pass.
